title.narrative: Drought in Displacement: Generating Evidence to Inform Responses to Urban Drought that are Inclusive of Displaced People in Dahiyyat Al-Malik Abdullah Neighbourhood, Mafraq City

description.narrative:
This project aims to tackle the critical issue of urban drought in the Dahiyyat Al-Malik Abdullah Neighbourhood, with a particular emphasis on the needs of refugees. The primary goal is to prioritize equitable water access in drought response strategies, urban planning, and policy formulation. By developing an evidence-based profile, the project will offer essential guidance for designing an efficient and sustainable water network capable of accommodating the neighborhood’s maximum expected population.
Our approach involves creating a comprehensive neighbourhood profile, conducting detailed studies and field investigations, and engaging with the local community to gather insights and foster participation. This process will enable us to identify necessary projects and provide detailed recommendations for water network infrastructure design and implementation.
Key accomplishments include enhancing local capacities for resilient planning, ensuring inclusive drought response strategies, and fostering sustainable development in the region. This project builds on previous collaborations between UN-Habitat Jordan and the Greater Mafraq Municipality (GMM) to improve access to basic services and the quality of life in Mafraq City. Leveraging the "Urban Planning and Infrastructure in Migration Contexts Programme," under which the Mafraq Spatial Profile was developed, UN-Habitat has identified Dahiyyat Al Malik Abdullah as one of the most vulnerable neighbourhoods due to the refugee influx and its impact on infrastructure.
Aligning with national and local priorities, this project aims to improve the quality of life for both host and refugee communities through the development of an evidence-based neighbourhood profile and water network design recommendations. By emphasizing capacity building and sustainable planning, the project seeks to ensure a resilient and inclusive approach to urban drought management, fostering long-term community resilience and equitable resource distribution.
